observation.visible_scene: A woman in a teal sports bra, light-gray leggings and white sneakers is on a patterned yoga mat in a sparse room with a white wall and gray floor. She holds a half-kneeling lunge: right knee and shin on the mat, left foot planted forward. A flat gray strap/resistance band loops under her front foot and she grips its upper end with both hands. Static props remain in place throughout: a green foam roller and gray kettlebell at the left wall, a pair of yellow and a pair of pink dumbbells at the right, and one pink dumbbell near the mat's right edge. The framing is fixed with no apparent camera movement.
visible_changes: Her head and upper torso tilt forward and downward from an upright, gaze-forward posture (frames ~1-9) to a rounded, head-down position looking toward her foot (frames ~13-30), then return toward upright with the head raised (frames ~35-41).

Her hands, initially held high near her chest with the strap nearly vertical, move downward and forward as she leans (strap top end drops and the strap tilts toward the front foot, frames ~13-30), then rise back up so the strap is again close to vertical (frames ~35-41).
The strap's lower end stays anchored under the front foot the whole time; only its upper end and angle change, i.e. the strap rotates/tilts rather than translating as a free object.
The lunge stance, foot placement, and all background equipment remain unchanged; the only motion is the woman's torso/head lean and the corresponding hand and strap movement.
The motion is continuous and already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last; it is a single back-and-tilt sequence, not a start-and-stop event.
outside_clip_unknowns: The purpose or name of the strap exercise and whether the lean-and-return is one rep of a set or a held stretch.
What occurs immediately before t=0 and after t=2.67 s, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
The actual tension in the strap and whether the band is elastic or a fixed handle.
uncertain_details: Whether the forward lean is an active movement or a gradual postural sag is not determinable from the frames alone.
Small frame-to-frame hand positions are hard to read precisely; the general down-then-up trajectory is clear but exact heights are approximate.
It is unclear if the strap tilts because she pulls it or simply because her hands move; no external force is visible.
